title: Quebecor makes $31B offer to acquire Telus
summary: Proposed deal will combine complementary networks, spectrum and operating capabilities, with Quebecor arguing the combined company would create a stronger telecom company for consumers.

image.caption: The Quebecor logo is seen at the company's head office, in Montreal in May 2024. (Ryan Remiorz/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Proposed deal will combine complementary networks, spectrum and operating capabilities, with Quebecor arguing the combined company would create a stronger telecom company for consumers.
Proposed deal would combine complementary networks, spectrum and operating capabilities
Quebecor has made a proposal worth $31 billion to take over Telus.

The telecom company said Monday in a news release it submitted a non-binding proposal to Telus in June to serve as a basis for negotiations. Telus is currently reviewing an enhanced proposal submitted by Quebecor earlier this month, according to the release.
The Montreal-based company says the proposed deal would combine complementary networks, spectrum and operating capabilities to strengthen investment capacity and competitive positioning.
Quebecor, Canada's fourth largest telecom company, argues that acquiring Telus would create a stronger company that could better serve consumers across the country.

"This proposal will create a strong pan-Canadian competitor, able to compete on equal terms with the other national providers and to stand up to foreign companies, for the benefit of Canadians," Quebecor said in the statement.
With files from The Canadian Press
